title: The Toll at the Burning Mountain
text: The road runs straight into a mountain on fire, and in front of it sits a king with an ox's horns and an iron cudgel across his knees. The heat bends the air around him. He offers strength for the toll every pilgrim pays: bow, and empty your purses at his feet.

options.label: Kneel in the heat and pay what he asks, for strength that will not fail you.

outcomes.text: The fire flows into your arms without burning. Your gold vanishes into the flames while the King's laughter shakes the mountain.

options.label: Refuse him to his horned face. No House of yours will bow to a demon.

outcomes.text: He rises, slow and enormous. Behind him the mountain roars higher in answer.

options.label: Take the gift and keep your purses, and hope he is slower than he looks.

outcomes.text: The Leader takes the fire but keeps the gold. The King only laughs, as though he means to collect later.
He was a demon long before he was a king. The fire turns inside the Leader's arms and burns them from within.
